ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (No. 8 of 1987, as amended) and International Companies Regulations 1998, together with the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (No. 23 of 2007, as amended) and its subordinate Money Laundering Prevention Regulations, constitute the core UBO and AML/CFT framework. The Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), the Registrar of International Companies, the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit exercise supervisory, licensing, and inspection mandates over licensed registered agents maintaining beneficial ownership records for Samoa International Companies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization — authentication by Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade followed by attestation at the destination Embassy or Consulate (Samoa is not a Hague Apostille Convention party)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended, requiring licensed registered agents and financial institutions to identify and verify all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories; mandatory screening against the Samoa FIU published list, United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List (ISIL/Da'esh and Al-Qaida, Taliban regimes), OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI Consolidated List, and Australian DFAT Consolidated Sanctions List; politically exposed persons require senior management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and enhanced ongoing monitoring; the bonded wine and spirits wholesale classification (ISIC 4632) triggers enhanced due diligence due to cross-border customs sensitivity, tax-exempt structuring, and higher money-laundering typology risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) — International Companies Registry; name clearance filings are effected electronically through the SIFA licensed registered agent portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English and Samoan are official languages. A Samoa International Company must be registered under an English-language corporate name; a Chinese trade name or secondary constitutional name may be adopted in the memorandum and articles, provided the English master text governs for statutory and registry purposes and a notarized Chinese translation is maintained with the registered agent. Transliteration of foreign names must use standard Latin-script romanization acceptable to the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name rejection must be communicated by the Registrar under the International Companies Act 1987. The applicant, acting through its licensed registered agent, may submit a written request for reconsideration within 14 days of the rejection notice, restating the proposed name and addressing the Registrar's stated grounds. If reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may file an administrative appeal to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 21 days of the reconsideration decision; the Minister's determination is final. A fresh name reservation, alternative name filing, or coexistence consent from an existing nameholder may also be lodged as a curative remedy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a Samoa International Company. The International Companies Act 1987 requires the company to maintain at all times a physical registered office in Samoa and a SIFA-licensed registered agent. A virtual office or digital service address cannot satisfy this statutory mandate; however, the licensed registered agent's physical Samoan office may serve as the registered office and commercial presence address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annual risk of unannounced SIFA or Financial Intelligence Unit on-site inspection is approximately 5% to 8% for a standard-risk International Company operating in the bonded wine and spirits wholesale sector, reflecting the enhanced due diligence tier assigned to ISIC 4632 customs-sensitive trade; compliant record-keeping materially reduces actual inspection exposure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987, as amended, Sections 7, 9, 12, 15, 26, and 31; Companies (Amendment) Acts; Customs Act 2008 for bonded licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association and Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an International Company; stated capital is fixed by the subscribers in the Memorandum and may be denominated in any currency; no escrow account is required at incorporation. A customs bond or bank guarantee is required to secure duties for bonded wine and spirits.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the incorporation application and Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed are ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the subscribers be allotted the shares set opposite their names. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the registered office at [address], Apia, Samoa is adopted and the Registered Agent is retained. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT [Directors] and [Secretary] are appointed as first directors and secretary. FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, file bonded warehouse license applications, and take all acts necessary to commence wine and spirits trading.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit name reservation request through the Companies Registry portal or in person at the Registry counter. The proposed name must end with 'International Company' or 'IC' and must not be deceptive, prohibited, or identical to an existing company. Payment of the name reservation fee is made at the cashier and the certificate is issued upon approval.
required_dossiers: Consent in writing for any restricted name element (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for resemblance, file a revised name application with a newly issued priority queue. If rejected due to a restricted word, obtain the responsible ministry's consent and resubmit within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Memorandum, Articles and Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Samoan Registered Agent to draft and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association. The documents must state the company type, capitalization structure and subscriber details. Each subscriber and director must execute a consent to act; all documents are then certified for filing.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or national ID of subscribers and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries missing authentication, arrange notarization or apostille in Samoa or in the jurisdiction of execution and resubmit the sworn declaration promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the signed Memorandum and Articles, consents, and the name reservation certificate. The Registry reviews the file, collects the prescribed filing fee, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon compliance with the International Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 duly signed by subscribers
Consent to act of directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned for correction, rectify the flagged provisions, re-execute any deficient signatures, and resubmit within 14 days; no additional penalty applies if cured in this window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent and Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board of directors meeting to approve the share allotment, adopt the registered office, appoint the first directors and secretary, and open the company's statutory registers. Issue share certificates and maintain registers of members, directors, and charges.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records are incomplete, the company secretary may submit a late filing of the missing register pages with a written explanation to the Registrar and pay the prescribed late filing fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs and Excise Registration for Bonded Wine and Spirits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority, Customs and Excise Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the bonded warehouse licensing application to the Samoa Revenue Authority along with evidence of incorporation, premises lease, security arrangements, and inventory control procedures. Obtain an importer/excise account and secure a customs bond or bank guarantee for deferred duty.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of licensed premises
Site security and inventory control plan
Customs Form C-50 or current equivalent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Customs and Excise Division issues a query, provide supplementary bank references and site security documentation, or request a hearing before the Commissioner within 21 days of the notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (Customs and Excise Division) and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (Trade and Commerce Division)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Bonded Warehouse Licence for Wines and Spirits, and General Liquor Wholesale Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Preliminary Environmental Assessment / Registration for nondischarging bonded warehouses; full EIA Report required if any wine blending, bottling, or effluent-producing operations are introduced
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with Samoa National Water Quality Standards; alcohol vapour and volatile organic compounds must meet National Air Quality Emission Limits; wine or spirit residues may not be discharged to stormwater drains and must be disposed of through a licensed waste contractor.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority; structural load inspection by a registered engineer for racking and storage areas; occupational safety and health registration and hazardous substances clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002 administered by MCIL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) - the national tax and customs administration of the Government of Samoa (successor to the Ministry for Revenue, 'Maota o Tupe Maua'), Apia; official e-services portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws; customs declarations and clearance via the ASYCUDA World single window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 through a licensed registered agent and local registered office at the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia; 2) Submit the TIN application (Form TIN-A) to the SRA with the Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent consent, director/shareholder particulars, and passport copies - statutory TIN is issued within 5-10 business days; 3) Register with Samoa Customs as an importer/exporter and obtain a Customs Client Code plus a Bonded Warehouse Operator Licence under the Customs Act 2014; 4) Register for VAGST (Form VR-1) only where the IC makes taxable supplies in Samoa exceeding SAT 200,000 (WST 200,000) per rolling 12 months - offshore-only ICs remain outside the VAGST net; 5) File the MCIL annual declaration and maintain the statutory tax-exemption status; no income tax return is required for the tax-exempt offshore business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - the Samoan International Company is statutorily a non-resident offshore entity exempt from income tax, stamp duty, and business licence fees under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), read with the Income Tax Ordinance 2015; the bonded wine/spirits export business is therefore outside the territorial income tax net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable - Samoa has no check-the-box or entity-classification election. Tax classification is fixed by statute: the International Company is non-resident and tax-exempt and cannot elect pass-through or entity-level taxation. No hybrid mismatch election is available. The only elective step is voluntary VAGST registration under the VAGST Act 2009 where the IC chooses to make domestic taxable supplies, plus the administrative application for a Certificate of Tax Exemption / tax-status confirmation letter from the SRA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) under the VAGST Act 2009; alcohol excise duty under the Customs Tariff Act 2014; customs duty and the bonded-warehouse suspension regime under the Customs Act 2014.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: SAT 200,000 (Samoa Tala / WST 200,000) of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period triggers compulsory VAGST registration (VAGST Act 2009, as amended); voluntary registration is available to non-resident and export-only suppliers. The bonded trader must in all cases hold Customs Client and excise-suspension registrations regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or Continuous Transaction Controls exist in Samoa. Registered VAGST suppliers must issue compliant tax invoices and preserve records for 7 years, with returns filed through the SRA e-services portal. All bonded movements and export declarations are lodged electronically in ASYCUDA World, which performs risk assessment and customs clearance; ASYCUDA lodgment is not a fiscal stamping regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and offshore supplies of services are zero-rated under the VAGST Act 2009. For bonded wine/spirits wholesale, 0% VAGST applies where: (a) the bonded goods physically depart Samoa under a Customs export declaration; (b) title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer; (c) the operator holds a valid Bonded Warehouse Operator Licence (Customs Act 2014) and Liquor Wholesale Licence (Sale of Liquor Act 2011); (d) removal occurs within the bond period such that excise duty is abated; and (e) the full documentary evidence bundle is retained. Input VAGST on freight, storage, and agency services attributable to export supplies is creditable or refundable through the SRA refund mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World) matched to the bonded removal permit
Bonded Warehouse Removal/Transfer Permit issued by Samoa Customs
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Samoa
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of origin/analysis (as applicable)
Bonded stock ledger and excise duty-suspension reconciliation report
Inward Foreign Currency Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT advice of payment from the non-resident buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Samoa Customs and the SRA may audit export and bond records for up to 7 years. If zero-rating is claimed without genuine export, bonded wine/spirits are diverted to domestic consumption, or the export proceeds are not received within 180 days: (i) the full 15% VAGST is assessed as output tax with monthly late-payment penalties and prescribed interest; (ii) excise duty is clawed back at the applicable spirits/wine rate plus a penalty not exceeding twice the duty; (iii) false declarations attract fines up to SAT 100,000 and/or imprisonment under the VAGST Act 2009 and Customs Act 2014, with aggravated evasion punishable by up to 7 years' imprisonment and forfeiture of goods; (iv) the IC's tax-exempt status, customs client code, and bonded warehouse licence may be revoked and the operator disqualified from future bonded facilities.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) / Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, Exchange Control Division - the sole monetary and foreign-exchange licensing authority in Samoa, operating under the Exchange Control Act 1976, Exchange Control Regulations 1977, Central Bank of Samoa Act 2003, Financial Institutions Act 1996, and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2017. The CBS grants all authorized-dealer licenses, approves capital-account transactions, maintains the external-account designation regime for non-resident International Companies, and supervises the Samoan International Finance Authority (SIFA) interface for IC corporate records.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a managed-float currency pegged by the CBS to a trade-weighted basket of the currencies of Samoa's major trading partners (USD, NZD, AUD, EUR, GBP, JPY, TWD) with active central-bank intervention. For current-account transactions - payments for genuine bonded wine purchases, storage, insurance, freight, and distributor commissions - the WST is freely convertible through licensed authorized dealers under the CBS general authority, requiring only documentary support (commercial invoice, warehouse release, transport documents) and the bank's standard AML/CFT checks. For capital-account transactions - initial equity subscription, shareholder subordinated loans, capital reductions, profit distributions, and redemption of shares - a prior CBS specific permit is mandatory; the authorized dealer files the application on behalf of the IC with board resolutions, source-of-funds documentation, and destination account details, with an observed approval cycle of 5 to 10 business days. Profit and dividend remittances by an exempt International Company carry no Samoan withholding tax, but the CBS requires a certificate of good standing from SIFA, a Ministry of Revenue tax-clearance confirmation (where applicable), and audited or CPA-reviewed management accounts demonstrating distributable profits derived exclusively from offshore bonded-trade activity. No domestic restriction applies to a non-resident IC holding foreign currency; the operating currency of the treasury should be USD/EUR/GBP because offshore WST liquidity is thin and the WST is not a deliverable settlement currency outside the Samoan banking system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1977, resident Samoan exporters must receive export proceeds through an authorized dealer within 90 days of shipment and surrender the full WST-equivalent to the banking system unless a surrender exemption is formally granted. For non-resident International Companies holding CBS external-account status, the applicable rules are materially different: (i) proceeds from bonded re-export trades must be credited to a CBS-approved external foreign-currency account at a Tier-1 authorized dealer (ANZ Bank Samoa or BSP Samoa) within 14 days of receipt from the buyer; (ii) no mandatory conversion into WST applies, so in practice 0% of bonded-trade proceeds are surrendered; (iii) every deposit must be accompanied by the trade invoice, warehouse release certificate, and transport document, retained for six years for CBS audit; and (iv) the IC must file an annual External Account Declaration reconciling all inbound and outbound trade flows through the authorized dealer. Balances in the external account may be freely remitted to bonded warehouse custodians, customs-bonded operators, insurers, and wholesale buyers worldwide without further CBS approval, provided the IC does not transact with Samoan residents and does not carry on business within the Samoan customs territory.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility with binding legal constraints. The CBS does not license electronic-money institutions or standalone third-party payment providers; the Financial Institutions Act 1996 restricts the taking of deposits and the operation of payment accounts to licensed commercial banks. Offshore digital EMIs cannot hold settlement accounts at Samoan banks, and CBS Exchange Control practice requires the IC to route all material inbound and outbound treasury flows through a Samoan authorized dealer in order to preserve the external-account audit trail and the capital-account evidence file. An offshore EMI may be used only as an auxiliary invoicing wallet in non-Samoan jurisdictions, provided it never holds IC share capital, never executes WST-denominated payments, and is not relied upon as the primary clearing rail; such an arrangement materially raises AML and correspondent-banking red flags and is not recommended as the primary treasury architecture. The preferred execution is a CBS-licensed multi-currency account at ANZ or BSP, complemented where necessary by a parallel EUR account at a Tier-1 EU bank connected through the same SWIFT infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Personal appearance is mandatory for initial onboarding. All Tier-1 Samoan banks require at least one director, the ultimate beneficial owner(s), and the appointed AML compliance officer to appear in person either (i) at the bank's head office in Apia for a board-level interview, or (ii) before a licensed Samoan registered agent who witnesses the execution of the account mandate and certification of identity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2017 verification standards. Remote-only and fully electronic onboarding is not permitted for non-resident companies; e-KYC is accepted only as a supplementary layer after physical verification is completed. A director located abroad may submit a certified identity pack executed before a notary public and apostilled, followed by a live video call, but the account mandate remains pending until the registered agent lodges the certified pack with the compliance department in Apia. The practical treasury plan should budget for a one-day Apia visit by the authorized signatory; consular legalization substitutes for the visit only under exceptional hardship and at the discretion of the CBS and the onboarding bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bonded wine and spirits trading is classified as a high-value, high-excise-risk commodity sector with potential smuggling, duty-evasion, and counterfeit-product predicates.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Valid bonded warehouse agreements with HMRC-accredited UK, French CRD/Douane, Spanish, and Hong Kong custodians; (2) excise suspension certificates (AAD / electronic movement documents) and customs entries for each specific parcel; (3) certificate of origin, chateau or distillery bills of lading, and maturing-whisky cask inventory registers; (4) a Bonded Trade Compliance Manual describing the internal control chain from intake, maturation, and insurance to final wholesale delivery; (5) complete counterparty KYC packs for all warehouse custodians and brokers; (6) annual serialized stock reconciliation reports for the aged Scotch and Bordeaux collection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity through discretionary trusts or legacy bearer-share structures historically associated with Samoan International Companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Samoan International Finance Authority (SIFA); (2) register of directors and register of shareholders maintained at the licensed registered agent; (3) statutory declaration under the International Companies Act 1987 confirming that no bearer shares are issued or outstanding; (4) beneficial ownership declaration (BOD) filed under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2017 showing the full economic-ownership chain to natural persons; (5) if trust-owned, the trust deed, protector register, and an independent legal opinion confirming the settlor's source of wealth; (6) a resident-agent introduction letter accepting accountability for the IC's statutory records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-tax jurisdiction matrix: a tax-exempt Samoa IC receiving and paying cross-border trade funds triggers tax-evasion, CRS, and financial-transparency adverse classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificate of Income-Tax Exemption under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) issued by SIFA and countersigned by the Ministry of Revenue; (2) non-resident tax-status certificate from the CBS or Ministry of Revenue confirming no domestic tax liability on bonded-trade income; (3) audited or CPA-reviewed financial statements for the wine-wholesale segment demonstrating that all economic activity occurs outside Samoa; (4) transfer-pricing documentation supporting intra-group mark-ups and sub-account interest; (5) a legal memorandum confirming that the IC is not a conduit or pass-through of Samoan-source income; (6) group structure chart and OECD CRS/EoIR self-certification forms for all shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control exposure: payments routed to bonded custodians and brokers across multiple jurisdictions, including the UK, EU, and Asia-Pacific venues.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Signed counterparty questionnaire identifying all warehouses, brokers, insurers, and final wholesale buyers; (2) evergreen sanctions and PEP screening output covering OFAC, EU, UK, UN, and APAC lists, generated by the bank's compliance screening engine; (3) relevant UK/EU wine and spirit licenses or customs-bonded operator authorizations; (4) destination-country alcohol import/export licenses and excise permits where applicable; (5) a signed undertaking that no Samoan resident person will be a counterparty, beneficiary, or recipient of IC funds, thereby preserving the external nature of the treasury.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity and shareholder-loan injections must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank cover) to the CBS-licensed external account at ANZ or BSP Samoa, with field 70 purpose narration reading 'SHARE SUBSCRIPTION WS_IC [date]' or 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN AGREEMENT [reference]'. The authorized dealer must receive, within five business days of credit, the board capitalization resolution, the share allotment form or executed loan agreement, and the source-of-funds declaration for the CBS capital-account record. In-kind capital contributions consisting of title to wine parcels in bonded warehouses are recognized as lawful IC assets; they are evidenced by an independent valuation report, the warehouse custodian's written confirmation of title transfer to WS_IC, and registration of the parcels in the IC's fixed-asset schedule held by the Samoan registered agent; no physical movement of goods to Samoa occurs. Escrowed subscription funds are released to the operating sub-ledger only after the CBS capital-import permit is issued; for loan injections, the interest rate, maturity, and repayment schedule must be declared on the authorized dealer's capital-import reporting form to prevent recharacterization of shareholder debt as equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: (1) Commercial Letters of Credit: for first-time supplier relationships, a confirmed irrevocable LC issued by ANZ or BSP Samoa in favor of the bonded warehouse custodian or fine-wine merchant, governed by UCP 600, requiring presentation of the warehouse release certificate, bonded stock number, and excise-suspension documents; this is the mandatory rail for purchases from new French and British merchants. (2) Open-account SWIFT MT103 wires from the IC external USD/EUR/GBP account to the supplier's clearing bank, with field 70 coded to the Bonded Parcel reference and field 72 referring to the purchase agreement; same-day value is achieved through the SWIFT network. (3) Intra-group and working-capital transfers to the IC's EU, UK, or Asia-Pacific sub-accounts are permitted under the external-account general authority if coded 'TRADE FINANCE - BONDED WINES' and supported by the underlying warehousing agreement. (4) Customs-security instruments: the authorized dealer may issue a demand guarantee or standby LC in favor of the revenue authority of the custody jurisdiction to support duty-suspended movements; such guarantees reduce the IC's approved facility limit and require trade-desk documentation. (5) All outbound wires must name the underlying beneficial owner, reference the bonded-trade number, and be captured in the annual External Account Declaration filed with the CBS.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CBS-approved outright deliverable forwards of up to 12 months tenor with ANZ Bank Samoa or BSP Samoa, executed only against genuine USD/EUR/GBP bonded-trade invoices and purchase orders; uncovered speculative positions are prohibited

Foreign-exchange forward rollover programs offered by authorized dealers for matching the GBP and EUR legs of vintage-cellar acquisitions, with warehouse collateral documents attached to each rollover

Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) with OECD-domiciled counterparties, permissible with prior CBS approval on a per-transaction basis where the notional exceeds USD 1,000,000 and the swap directly hedges the IC's bond facility or shareholder loan
Vanilla FX options (puts and calls) as hedges of the estimated resale value of euro-denominated Bordeaux and Scotch portfolios, subject to a CBS derivative-specific exemption per transaction

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on third currencies (e.g., USD/HKD for Asian wholesale settlements) are permissible only where the bond-trade invoice is non-deliverable in nature and the counterparty is an OECD bank; NDFs referencing the WST are prohibited for International Company treasuries

Natural-currency matching as a zero-cost hedge: maintain parallel USD and EUR external sub-ledgers to eliminate conversion risk, with temporary tenor gaps covered by interest-bearing deposits at the authorized dealer capped at 5% of operating liquidity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late-filing surcharge is imposed on overdue fees; failure to remedy within the grace period permits the Registrar to strike the company off the International Companies Register following notice in the Samoa Gazette, resulting in loss of corporate personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the International Company Annual Return within 30 days after each incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Included in the annual return obligation; omission is treated as an incomplete filing and attracts the same late-filing surcharge, with the company subject to strike-off for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Liquor and Bonded Warehouse Trade Licence Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Customs and Revenue (Samoa Revenue Corporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 December, or before the expiry date of the existing licence, whichever is earlier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal suspends bonded warehouse operations and releases excise obligations; continued operation without a valid licence attracts excise default penalties and possible cancellation of the customs bonded status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to an ordinary Samoa International Company. A mandatory audit is triggered only if the company is licensed under a regulated financial services statute, such as offshore banking or international insurance, or if its constitutional documents require an audit. A bonded wine and spirits wholesale trading company falls outside the statutory audit class, and the appointment of an auditor is voluntary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No Samoa local GAAP is prescribed for International Companies. Financial records must be maintained on a true and fair basis; IFRS is the recognised benchmark where voluntary financial statements are prepared. The company must retain records sufficient to explain transactions and to enable the financial position to be determined with reasonable accuracy.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Beneficial Owners must be kept at the company's registered office in Samoa and updated upon each transfer of shares or change of ownership. An annual confirmation of beneficial ownership is filed together with the Annual Return and is certified by a director or the registered agent. The confirmation restates the name, residential address, and ownership percentage of each beneficial owner as at the incorporation anniversary and records any shareholding transfers completed during the preceding year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - 3,000 per engagement (if a voluntary certified audit is commissioned)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (Income Tax Act 2012, as amended). A licensed Samoa International Company (IC) is statutorily exempt from income tax, stamp duty and exchange control under s.209 of the International Companies Act 2008 while it remains non-resident in conduct and derives no Samoa-source income, resulting in a 0% effective tax rate for the bonded trade.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% for a qualifying IC on income derived and operations conducted outside Samoa; no separate tax holiday is granted for bonded wine/spirit distribution, and the annual IC government fee (scaled by deemed capital) is the principal impost. A taxable Samoan branch would be assessed at 27% on Samoa-source profit and may claim the 5-year loss carry-forward.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (prescribed Form IC-AR) and annual government fee statement lodged with the Samoa Registrar of International Companies through the e-Samoa Registry portal of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and fee payment are due within 60 days following each anniversary of incorporation; no financial statements are required for an exempt IC, but an economic substance declaration is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: registration number, registered name, date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete in English; a Samoan TRN is not required for an exempt IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoan registered office address and licensed registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed Samoan agent must remain appointed and must countersign the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorised capital, deemed capital, issued shares, and share classes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deemed capital drives the annual fee; no minimum capital is imposed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemption declaration: no business within Samoa; all bonded-trade contracts and revenues attributable outside Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Sales invoices, warehouse receipts and delivery documents must evidence offshore sourcing and destination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Register of directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Agent holds KYC identity and address records for all beneficial owners and produces them to the Financial Intelligence Unit on request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late return: WST 200 fixed penalty plus WST 50 per day (capped at WST 5,000); overdue annual fee carries 10% per annum interest; sustained default triggers strike-off from the Register and loss of the income tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Samoa Company Income Tax Return (Company Annual Return, prescribed by the Ministry for Revenue) filed through the national e-file portal; required for any IC that has lost or never qualified for the exemption, operates a Samoa permanent establishment, or derives Samoa-source income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The income year ends 31 December; the return is due on or before 31 March of the following year (or within six months after an approved substituted accounting period).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income, exempt income, and assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report bonded wholesale turnover separately; Samoan domestic deliveries are assessable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: cost of goods sold, distribution costs, depreciation, interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach audited financial statements; costs allocable to non-Samoan revenue are non-deductible.
Apply the five-year loss carry-forward where admissible.
Only profits attributable to the Samoan permanent establishment are taxed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and treaty credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Ministry for Revenue tax residence certificate and DTA relief schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax instalments, balance payable/refund, declaration by director/agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident branches settle quarterly instalments by 30 March, 30 June, 30 September and 30 December.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of tax payable (minimum WST 700) plus 10% per annum interest; false or misleading returns incur a 100% shortfall penalty, fines up to WST 200,000, and imprisonment up to seven years for fraudulent evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% final withholding tax under the Income Tax Act 2012 on dividends paid by a Samoa resident company to non-resident shareholders. Dividends distributed by a qualifying International Company to non-resident shareholders are exempt from Samoan tax and paid without WHT deduction while the IC licence and non-residence conditions are continuously satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand double tax agreement relief: (1) obtain a Samoa Tax Residence Certificate on the prescribed application form with certified incorporation documents; (2) obtain the foreign shareholder's residence certificate and execute a beneficial-ownership declaration before the dividend date; (3) apply the treaty rate at source and file an annual reconciliation schedule with the Ministry for Revenue. The treaty dividend ceiling is 5% where the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of voting power and 15% otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest 15%, royalties 10%. Treaty-reduced rates under both Samoan DTAs: interest 10%, royalties 10%. A qualifying IC owes no withholding on interest or royalties referable to business carried on wholly outside Samoa.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File documentation is required where aggregate related-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000 per income year; Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 or more under Samoa's BEPS Inclusive Framework commitments; below threshold, the Ministry for Revenue may still compel a transfer-pricing study by information notice.
